cards.definition: A kind action that you do for someone because they asked.
cards.example:
- Could you do me a favor and forward that email to me?
Você poderia me fazer um favor e encaminhar aquele e-mail?
cards.note: Do someone a favor. No inglês britânico escreve-se favour.

cards.definition: To be annoyed or bothered by something.
cards.example:
- Would you mind sending the file again? I lost the first one.
Você se importaria de enviar o arquivo de novo? Perdi o primeiro.
cards.note: Would you mind + verbo -ing. Atenção: “No, I don't mind” = SIM, pode.

cards.definition: To be grateful for something someone does.
cards.example:
- I would appreciate a quick answer before the end of the day.
Eu agradeceria uma resposta rápida até o fim do dia.
cards.note: I'd appreciate it if you could… é o pedido mais elegante do inglês corporativo.

cards.example:
- Sorry to bother you, but the client is asking about the deadline.
Desculpe incomodar, mas o cliente está perguntando do prazo.
cards.note: Sorry to bother you abre qualquer interrupção educada.

cards.definition: To say you are willing to do or give something.
cards.example:
- She offered to review my presentation before the meeting.
Ela se ofereceu para revisar minha apresentação antes da reunião.
cards.note: Offer TO + verbo: offer to help.

cards.definition: Behaving in a way that shows respect for other people.
cards.example:
- In English, polite language is expected, not optional.
Em inglês, linguagem educada é esperada, não opcional.

cards.definition: A very polite way of asking someone to do something.
cards.example:
- Would you mind joining the call ten minutes earlier?
Você se importaria de entrar na reunião dez minutos mais cedo?
cards.note: Sempre com verbo -ing. Resposta positiva: Not at all!

cards.translation: eu queria saber se… / será que você poderia…
cards.definition: A soft, indirect way of introducing a request.
cards.example:
- I was wondering if you could check these numbers today.
Eu queria saber se você poderia conferir estes números hoje.
cards.note: O pedido mais suave que existe. Use com chefes e clientes novos.

cards.definition: Extremely beautiful, refined or of very high quality.
cards.example:
- The hotel served an exquisite dinner for the whole team.
O hotel serviu um jantar requintado para a equipe inteira.
cards.note: “Esquisito” (estranho) é weird ou strange. Exquisite é elogio!

cards.definition: Trying to seem more important or clever than you really are.
cards.example:
- His email sounded pretentious, not confident.
O e-mail dele soou pretensioso, não confiante.
cards.note: “Pretensioso” no sentido de ambicioso é ambitious. Pretentious é sempre negativo.

questions.prompt: You ask a colleague for a small kindness. You say:
options: Could you do me a favor?
Could you make me a favor?
Could you do me a favour please me?
Could you give me a favor?
questions.answer: Could you do me a favor?
questions.explanation: You DO a favor. The Portuguese “fazer” tempts “make”.

options: Would you mind sending the file?
Would you mind to send the file?
Would you mind send the file?
Would you mind that send the file?
questions.answer: Would you mind sending the file?
questions.explanation: “Mind” takes -ing. And careful: “not at all” means yes, they will do it.

questions.prompt: I'd _____ it if you could confirm before the end of the day.
questions.explanation: “Appreciate” needs an object: “I'd appreciate it if…”.

questions.prompt: Sorry to _____ you, but the client is asking about the deadline.
questions.explanation: “Sorry to bother you” is said before the trouble; “sorry for bothering” comes after.

questions.prompt: Ela se ofereceu para revisar minha apresentação antes da reunião.
questions.answer: She offered to review my presentation before the meeting.|She offered to check my presentation before the meeting.

questions.prompt: In English, _____ language is expected, not optional.
_____ sending the file again? I lost the first one.
questions.explanation: The softest of the request forms; -ing follows.

questions.prompt: _____ you could take a look at this before Friday.
questions.explanation: The past tense makes the request softer, even about now.

questions.prompt: The dessert was of the highest quality. It was…
He tries to look cleverer than he is. He is…
questions.explanation: “Pretentious” is showing off. To plan something is “intend”, not “pretend”.
